reports.title: Oaktree Specialty Lending Corporation Announces Fourth Fiscal Quarter and Full Year 2026 Financial Results

desk.headline: Investment income down 12% to $68.2m, slight miss; adjusted NII $0.34 a share, in line; $0.32 payout declared, no guidance

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted net investment income per share; GAAP NII $0.34 vs $0.41

other.label: Net asset value per share
other.change: vs $15.70 in June; $16.64 a year ago

results: Total investment income fell to $68.2m from $77.3m a year earlier, on lower interest rates and a smaller loan book.
Adjusted net investment income was $29.6m, or $0.34 a share, down from $0.37 last quarter and $0.40 a year ago, partly due to higher incentive fees.
Net asset value per share eased to $15.63 after $7.2m of net losses on investments.
Credit improved over the year: loans not paying interest fell to 1.8% of the debt book at fair value from 3.0%, with six problem loans versus ten.
New commitments of $178.5m were outpaced by $197.8m of repayments; a $300m five-year bond was issued in September and liquidity stands at about $1.04bn.

guidance.summary: No earnings guidance. The board declared a $0.32 distribution ($0.30 base plus $0.02 supplemental) payable 31 Dec 2026.

points: Management highlighted the drop in non-accrual loans and said new problems are company-specific, not industry-wide; Pluralsight and BioXcel were added to the list.
Higher short-term interest rates should start lifting income from the December quarter, since almost all loans are floating-rate.
Software is about 20% of the portfolio, mostly first-lien; loans seen at high risk from AI disruption are about 3% of performing debt.
The 2027 notes will be repaid from the credit line in January; the new 7% bond adds a small extra interest cost.
The $0.30 base dividend was reset in May so that earnings cover it at current debt levels; lending out spare cash comes before any share buybacks.
call.source: Call coverage: The Motley Fool call transcript, 17 Nov 2026; results presentation filed as Exhibit 99.2

watch: Whether higher rates lift NII back above the $0.30 base distribution with room to spare.
Progress on the six non-accrual loans, including Pluralsight.
Net asset value trend and the pace of new lending versus repayments.
